R0216.title: Virtual Asset Cross-Platform Transfer Risk
R0216.definition: Virtual asset interoperability protocols between metaverse platforms have vulnerabilities that may cause asset transfer failures, double-spending or theft.

references.title: Interoperability security for metaverse virtual assets

R0216.description:
Virtual asset cross-platform transfer risk appears when assets move across metaverse platforms, games, wallets, or marketplaces. When interoperability protocols have flaws in asset custody, state synchronization, or permission verification, attackers can craft cross-platform transfer requests to trigger double spend, asset loss, or theft — for example, a bridge contract that does not atomically bind source-chain burn to target-chain minting, leaving the same asset valid on both chains.

Interoperability increases liquidity but connects the trust boundaries of multiple platforms. Once any platform's custodial private key, signing authority, or oracle feed is compromised, losses propagate along mapping relationships to all interconnected platforms. Designs must clarify custodial liability, finality windows, exception rollback, and dispute handling, and constrain transfer paths through cross-chain verification (A0189), bridge audits (A0102), and virtual-asset cross-chain verification (A0164).
R0216.influence: Once a cross-platform transfer shows double spend or theft, users lose virtual assets directly and the platform bears compensation and trust loss; interoperability-protocol flaws propagate along mapping relationships to all interconnected platforms, triggering cascading asset-security incidents and undermining confidence in the metaverse asset-interoperability system.

observables: Cross-platform asset transfers show state-sync failures or double spends
Interoperability protocols complete asset flows under insufficient permission verification
Asset mapping relationships in cross-platform transfers show inconsistencies
Failure or rollback mechanisms fail to trigger correctly under anomalous conditions
Cross-platform asset custody and eventual consistency show persistent divergence
